ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the Gulf of Mexico and its surrounding areas, with “Gulf of Mexico” marked in the center. On the right, the Florida Peninsula and nearby sea areas can be seen. The figure has latitude and longitude markings such as the 20°N latitude line and meridians near 90°; location B is located along the coast of the Gulf of Mexico, in a low-latitude coastal area near Florida. Then reason: The question limits the inquiry to the “low-temperature natural disaster” mainly affecting location B. Although the Gulf of Mexico coast and the Florida area are at relatively low latitudes and have a relatively warm climate, in winter they are sometimes affected by southward-moving North American cold air, causing crops or vegetation to suffer low-temperature freezing damage. This type of low-temperature natural disaster corresponds to “freezing damage.”
